definition.description: Accelerate through a declared linear approach, brake before a marked turn line, plant the declared turn foot, reorient the whole body 180 degrees, and reaccelerate through the opposite-direction exit. One repetition contains one approach, one planned 180-degree turn, and one exit. Approach and exit distance, plant side, pivot strategy, and timing context are declared delivery variables. This excludes reactive cues, a second turn, 5-10-5, jumps, and a terminal stick.

environment.surface: clear, level, dry, high-traction non-slip lane with protected braking, turn, exit, and runoff space
environment.space: one protected measured approach, turn marker, exit lane, and safe finish zone without cross traffic
inspection: surface traction, debris, weather, footwear, marker visibility, and lane separation
approach, turn, exit, and runoff geometry
environment.changeRule: Changing approach or exit distance, entry speed, turn foot, pivot strategy, marker, surface, timing, cue, intent, dose, or symptoms requires revalidation.

selectionPrerequisites: pain-free linear acceleration and progressive deceleration
owns lower-speed planned 180-degree turns on both plant sides
session sprint, braking, change-of-direction, and technical-fatigue budgets fit
excludeOrEscalate: pain, guarding, slip, unsafe lane, repeated line overrun, collapse, balance loss, or communication conflict
new neurologic, circulation, breathing, chest, balance, or coordination concern
notEstablishedByEvidence: universal approach distance, pivot strategy, dose, recovery, testing norm, performance outcome, readiness threshold, or clinical clearance

provenance.identityAuthority: Source 160 plus the focused 180-degree transitions packet: one planned approach, brake, turn, and reacceleration is the stable identity; Modified/Traditional 505 are controlled contexts and reactive or multi-turn routes are distinct.

anatomy.laterality: record turn foot and side; program both planned plant sides rather than assuming equivalence
anatomy.claimsBoundary: Describes task mechanics and plausible loading sites only; it does not diagnose, treat, prevent injury, or guarantee agility or sport transfer.

athleteSupport.whyItMatters: Candidate planned braking, turning, and exit practice only when the exact lane, entry speed, plant side, and total change-of-direction budget fit.
athleteSupport.primaryCue: Brake before the line, plant and turn your whole body, then push cleanly into the exit.
secondaryCues: lower through the final approach steps rather than one late brake
hit the declared turn zone with the assigned foot
do not slip, collapse, or add a false exit step
use the full recovery and report symptoms
expectedSensations: substantial lower-body braking and push-off effort
brief high-attention plant, reorientation, and exit
unexpectedSensations: pain, slip, knee or trunk collapse, groin discomfort, dizziness, inability to brake, or marked side difference
selfChecks: turn foot hit the target zone

observationChecklist: exact approach/turn/exit geometry and entry speed
turn foot, line contact, knee/trunk control, rotation, first exit steps, and side asymmetry
surface, symptoms, timing when used, recovery, and total COD exposure

faultCorrections.late_braking: shorten or slow approach and restore braking before the final plant
faultCorrections.plant_slip_or_collapse: stop, inspect surface/footwear, reduce entry speed, and rebuild lower-speed turn control
faultCorrections.false_exit_step: reduce entry speed and rehearse full-body reorientation before accepting speed
faultCorrections.line_overrun: shorten approach or add marker guidance; do not chase timing

doNotUseWhen: the intended task is reactive, multi-turn, 5-10-5, jump-to-turn, or terminal-stick work
surface, braking readiness, symptoms, lane, recovery, supervision, or communication is inadequate

supportOperations.supportEscalation: Stop and escalate unresolved pain, slips, collapse, asymmetry, unsafe conditions, or a mismatch between requested and exact planned single-turn task.
supportOperations.changeImpactPolicy: Any change to approach, exit, speed, marker, turn side, surface, cue, dose, timing, or substitute reruns selection, fatigue, impact, logistics, duration, substitutions, and validation.

sourceVariant.archiveReason: The source lacks approach/exit geometry, turn foot, pivot strategy, valid line contact, dose, load, fatigue, and review contracts.

legacy.description: Planned linear approach, braking, planted 180-degree turn, and opposite-direction reacceleration.
legacy.tempo: brake before line; one planned half-turn; clean exit; full recovery
legacy.loadNote: High-rate bodyweight braking and reacceleration; exact entry speed, distance, and rest are delivery-profile specific.
legacy.cardSummary: Candidate planned 180-degree turn-and-reaccelerate card with exact lane, plant, braking, exit, and stop boundaries.
legacy.coachLanguage: Measure the lane, protect braking/plant quality and side balance, and end before speed or control declines.
legacy.athleteLanguage: Brake early, plant and turn the whole body, exit cleanly, recover fully, and report symptoms.

safety.prerequisiteNotes: Readiness is the exact approach speed, braking, plant, lane, surface, symptoms, and recovery context—not a participant classification.
readinessChecks: lower-speed 180-degree turn control on both sides
clear high-traction lane and finish zone
stopSigns: pain, guarding, slip, plant collapse, repeated overrun, balance loss, unsafe lane, marked asymmetry, speed loss, or participant stop request
fatigue that prevents controlled braking and clean first exit steps
contraindications: symptom, unsafe surface, inadequate braking or plant control, recovery, supervision, or communication
reactive cue, multi-turn route, jump, terminal stick, or testing protocol without a separately reviewed contract
commonSubstitutions: Use another reviewed task only after full revalidation.
Do not automatically substitute reactive 180s, 5-10-5, a jump turn, or braking-only work.

score.reviewNotes: Candidate task-only reassessment from 180-degree biomechanics and deceleration evidence; independent calibration remains required.

difficultyProfile.notes: Exact planned single 180-degree turn-and-reaccelerate contract only.

deliveryProfiles.purpose: Candidate lower-speed planned 180-degree braking, plant, reorientation, and exit rehearsal.

dosage.countRule: count only a controlled approach, braking before marker, valid turn-foot plant, one 180-degree turn, aligned exit, and safe stop

deliveryProfiles.qualityGate: Braking begins before the marker, plant remains in the valid zone without slip/collapse, the body reorients to exit, first exit steps are clean, and no stop symptom occurs.
stopRules: stop for pain, slip, collapse, balance loss, unsafe lane, or participant request
stop when braking, plant, or exit control cannot be restored with lower speed and rest
deliveryProfiles.coachInstructions: Measure and inspect lane, declare plant side and speed, observe final approach contacts and exit, balance sides, and end before turning practice becomes fatigued conditioning.
deliveryProfiles.athleteInstructions: Approach at the assigned speed, brake before the line, plant and turn the whole body, push into the exit, and take the full recovery.
deliveryProfiles.expectedAdaptation: Candidate planned turn coordination only; no guaranteed agility or sport outcome is claimed.

doseScaling.reduce: shorten approach/exit, lower entry speed, reduce repetitions, increase rest, or use another reviewed task after revalidation
doseScaling.doNotAutoProgress: Do not add cue uncertainty, a second turn, a jump, higher speed, longer approach, or testing automatically.

supportPrompts.athlete: Brake early, one turn, clean exit.
supportPrompts.coach: Protect plant and exit quality before speed.

deliveryProfiles.purpose: Candidate high-intent planned single-turn braking and reacceleration output with full recovery.

dosage.countRule: count only exact planned approach, brake, single planted 180, opposite-direction exit, and safe run-through

deliveryProfiles.qualityGate: Entry speed, braking, valid plant, turn, exit, side control, lane safety, and symptoms remain acceptable; no repeated overrun, slip, collapse, false step, or visible speed decline occurs.
stopRules: stop for any movement-intelligence stop rule
stop when high-speed braking or first exit steps lose quality despite full recovery
stop rather than turning this into multi-turn conditioning
deliveryProfiles.coachInstructions: Use only after lower-speed ownership; protect lane, plant-side balance, exposure, and recovery, and record distance, turn foot, quality, symptoms, and timing only when the protocol is declared.
deliveryProfiles.athleteInstructions: Use the planned lane and side, brake before the marker, turn once, drive the exit cleanly, run through safely, and recover fully.
deliveryProfiles.expectedAdaptation: Candidate planned high-intent COD exposure only; no guaranteed performance outcome is claimed.

doseScaling.reduce: reduce entry speed, approach/exit, repetitions, or increase rest; use another reviewed task after revalidation
doseScaling.doNotAutoProgress: Do not add reaction, multiple turns, jumping, a flying 505 approach, or time trial status automatically.

supportPrompts.athlete: One planned turn, clean exit, full rest.
supportPrompts.coach: Entry speed and turn quality are both dose variables.
